author: Hailey Pitcher
title: Hilton Horizons Academy aims to further enrich homeschooled students - NewsBreak
text:
By Hailey Pitcher ,
2 hours ago
KINGSPORT, Tenn. (WJHL) – Last year, Candice Hilton made the decision to homeschool her daughter. She felt the public school structure didn’t provide the flexibility and enrichment her daughter needed.
Hilton, a former public school teacher, started the Hilton Horizons Academ y, a K-12 “hybrid microschool” that offers programming to support homeschooled students. The academy teaches core courses, such as reading and math, along with enrichment courses, such as STEM, art and Spanish.
“We have our abstract artist who comes in and teaches art classes,” said Hilton. “We have small town makers who comes in and teaches STEM, and we also bring in like local community members. We had Sparky the Dog from the fire department, and the kids loved that. We’ve had visitors from NASA, we’ve had visitors from Build Advantage, tons of places. It teaches kids that they have options for careers, and it makes sure that they learn hands-on lessons.”
The Hilton Horizons Academy currently teaches 40 students and has two locations: one in Kingsport, which opened in July, and another in Johnson City, which opened in September. The program currently staffs three teachers, including Hilton herself, and three members of enrichment staff.
“Our program is two days, three days or five days,” Hilton said. “If they came to us on a two-day program, for example, then the other three days, they would be homeschooling at home, so this really does help parents to keep the flexibility that they love with homeschooling while also getting the support from teachers and tutoring services and socialization for their kids.”
Hilton said the program includes core subjects in the morning, an hour lunch break and options for enrichment classes in the afternoon.
Students take field trips and are given the option to focus on subjects that interest them.
The program makes sure that each student is getting their individual academic needs met through MAP testing and private tutoring sessions.
“It’s a very supportive network,” Hilton said. “I think that is something you would not find in public school, as well as the fact that, not only are we connected in a social aspect, but we’re connected to their academics. We set goals together. We love what we’re doing, and we place on growing our program, and we just hope to continue to see the progress that we’re making.”
